summary: A dense civilization game where you draft dice onto a shared programming/council board, using low-value dice to unlock stronger actions and high-value dice to advance on a turn-order track; over four rounds you build cities and monuments, run trade routes, research decrees, and jockey for area influence around Knossos. It plays like a heavier cousin of the designer's earlier Rurik: Dawn of Kiev, trading direct conflict for economic and positional competition.
praised: Clever dice-drafting/programming system that rewards planning several actions ahead
Strong table presence and production quality
Meaningful variable player powers and setup that change strategy each game
Satisfying multi-path economic engine building (trade, monuments, decrees)
criticised: High rules overhead and long teach for a first play
Analysis paralysis from the dice-programming puzzle, especially in higher player counts
Some imbalance/luck perceived in dice rolls despite the drafting mitigation
Runtime can drag past the stated 90-150 minutes

interaction.kind: area majority/influence and dice drafting with some blocking, plus limited direct conflict against outsiders

scoring.why: victory points accumulate from multiple systems at once—city/monument building, area majority, trade routes, and decrees—so the winner is usually whoever balances several engines rather than maxing one

_name: Minos: Dawn of the Bronze Age
